properties.source: al-Idrīsī as edited by Dozy and de Goeje (1866); Ecoregions 2017 (RESOLVE), shapefile, version 2017, archive of 7 May 2019, https://storage.googleapis.com/teow2016/Ecoregions2017.zip, SHA-256 be36d6209e443038d02e309f0447c6e7f2a62f5fe60c605ffe90d064952f2a60; Natural Earth 1:50m Cultural Vectors, Admin 0 Countries, version 5.1.2, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector/v5.1.2/geojson/ne_50m_admin_0_countries.geojson, SHA-256 3e458fc036ad0a66411f2c1e6cac49c5d7bfb81cb1123bc513b22511a2b7fdeb; Natural Earth 1:10m Physical Vectors, Rivers + lake centerlines, version 5.1.2, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector/v5.1.2/geojson/ne_10m_rivers_lake_centerlines.geojson, SHA-256 bb854a900ecbd3b408df46d5e16e3e0f974ba55993f9d8b5c26e855273c0905a
properties.citation: al-Idrīsī, Nuzhat al-mushtāq fī ikhtirāq al-āfāq (1154), first climate, second section, on Ghana, in R. Dozy and M. J. de Goeje (eds., trans.), Description de l'Afrique et de l'Espagne par Edrîsî, Leiden, Brill, 1866, French translation p. 9: « Le pays de Ghana touche […] au nord au grand désert (Sahara) qui sépare le Soudan du pays des Berbers ». The gloss « (Sahara) » is the translators'.
properties.derivation: Built by social/video/areas.mjs: Africa's land north of the Sahara in its own grid column, between the desert and the Mediterranean or the Atlantic, outside Egypt (Natural Earth Admin 0, ADM0_A3 EGY) and west of the Nile; the Sahara is the union of the Ecoregions 2017 ecoregions Saharan Atlantic coastal desert, North Saharan Xeric Steppe and Woodland, West Sahara desert, East Sahara Desert, South Sahara desert, West Saharan montane xeric woodlands, East Saharan montane xeric woodlands, Tibesti-Jebel Uweinat montane xeric woodlands, Saharan halophytics, on Africa's land (Africa's land is the union of the Natural Earth Admin 0 countries whose CONTINENT is Africa); « west of the Nile » keeps, on each grid row, the cells west of the westernmost crossing of the Natural Earth rivers named Nile, El Bahr el Abyad or Bahr el Jebel; north of the river's last vertex (the delta apex near Cairo) the apex longitude is used; on a 0.05° grid (cells whose centre falls inside), traced back as the cell boundary, simplified by Douglas–Peucker at 0.05° and rounded to 0.01°; parts and holes under 5000 km² dropped. This is EthniAfrica's reconstruction of a medieval description, not a border: al-Idrīsī drew no line between these lands. Berber-speaking peoples also lived in the desert itself (the veiled Ṣanhāja of the Arabic geographers); this area leaves them to the desert.
